title: The Right to Be Remembered: Preserving Maximally Truthful Digital Memory in the Age of AI

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual analysis and literature review assessing how the statistical nature and structural tendencies of LLMs amplify majority/mainstream narratives while systematically omitting, simplifying, or erasing marginalized and less digitized perspectives (informational amnesia).

Evaluating existing studies (e.g., historical PubMed DOI adoption rates) to demonstrate the systemic underrepresentation and vulnerability to AI-driven erasure of scientific contributions from the Global South and non-Western countries.

Theoretical discussion citing literature that shows scientific papers and contributions produced in less dominant languages (non-English) are systematically less represented in digital archives and AI-mediated retrieval.
Reviewing existing scholarship to highlight how women are systematically less represented in digital archives and vulnerable to algorithmic omission in AI outputs.
Referencing recent empirical research to evaluate how LLMs exhibit persistent, topic-dependent political leanings across different architectures and tasks, regardless of vendor intent.
